real_task: Prepare the private evidence plan for the first planned AI FOR AI LAB channel episode before any rendering or upload work.
task_origin: The owner-directed channel was already recorded in Session 021; merged Session 024 and the completed cross-agent tool-discovery exchange now provide a concrete story that exists independently of publisher-check.
candidate_story: The owner imposed a golden transparency rule, while the two agents independently challenged and then parked a weakly supported optimization direction.

evidence_map.premise: Human intervention must be disclosed, with safety and excessive cost as the stated limits.
Agent 2 challenged the tool-discovery baseline and Agent 1's follow-up led the gate to park the family.

baseline: A manually selected topic and repository references with no machine-readable boundary receipt; zero unsafe or unsupported choices were machine-detected.
hypothesis: Running publisher-check on the real private plan catches at least one missing evidence or audience-to-research boundary problem before production, if one is present.
quality_control: Independently inspect that both candidate-story premises have direct local references, keep the plan private and human-reviewed, and preserve all tests. A valid receipt alone is not a quality pass for a future script.
overhead: Count plan authoring, evidence inspection, validator invocation, reporting, documentation, tests and checkpoint maintenance. No renderer, network, secret, paid API or upload.
stop_condition: Run the frozen validator once. Do not add fields or product code in this session; report zero findings as inconclusive rather than manufacture a violation.

failures: The initial plan cited broad docs/DECISIONS.md. Recording this evaluation changed that file's hash on the verification run, immediately aging the receipt and exposing a partly circular dependency. The redundant ref was removed in favor of the two specific observation traces, requiring an extra validation invocation.
limitations: The seven-field plan contains no title, claims, script or shot text, so the validator had no narrative statement to judge.
A valid receipt establishes declared bytes and boundary values only; it cannot show that the later story uses those bytes faithfully.
There was no naturally unsafe or audience-driven choice in this plan, so zero findings cannot distinguish a useful gate from a no-op.
publisher-check did not identify the broad mutable evidence reference; manual workflow review did.
Elapsed time and token overhead were not measured comparably; authored files, calls, tests and checkpoint maintenance are recorded instead.
result.reason: Keep version 1 as a narrow boundary receipt. Do not expand its schema or build channel infrastructure until an actual story or script can receive independent evidence review.
